newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent stays soft but considered under-valued.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent stays soft but considered under-valued.

text.p: North Sea Brent spot and paper markets were soft on Thursday, but prices for other grades held steady in relation to wet Brent's deep discounts.
After a flurry of trade in the low thirties for late Jan early Feb Forties barrels on Wednesday, sellers considered the market under-valued in relation to Dated Brent.
One trader said the he felt a U.S. trade house's end month pricing strategy was keeping the Brent market down.
"He (the trade house) has bought several Brent cargoes this week and sold them on to a U.S. trader who is taking them transatlantic," one Forties equity holder said.
He said the same player was still offering Dated Brent down to Feb Brent -24 cents but thought the physical market was looking better balanced after active trade this week.
However, weaker Brent futures and narrowing paper spreads continued to fuel bearish sentiment, traders said.
"I think the market is at least going to stay down at these sort of levels and perhaps go lower," one said.
Differentials for other North Sea grades such as Oseberg and Statfjord continued supported by the knock-on effect of production problems at Norway's Ekofisk field.

Ekofisk operator Phillips said on Thursday that it expected to resume production at the 350,000 barrel per day field at the weekend after it was shut in early on Tuesday because of a gas leak in a pipeline.
No Brent dates were due to turn wet on Thursday. The first dates from the February programme will emerge on Friday.
Brent intermonth spreads firmed a little, but were easing back towards earlier, lower levels in late business.
Feb/Mar traded at +33, up to +35 cents and valued around +$32 in late business with Mar/April and Apr/May offered at +45 cents.
